Review Text: A profound masterpiece about the resilience of the human spirit. The chemistry between Robbins and Freeman is legendary, and the ending is perhaps the most satisfying in cinematic history.
The pinnacle of crime drama. Coppola's direction and Brando's performance create a haunting, beautiful portrait of power and family that has never been surpassed.
Nolan redefined the superhero genre. Ledger’s Joker is a chaotic force of nature that makes this more of a high-stakes crime thriller than a comic book movie.
The greatest character study ever televised. Watching Walter White’s slow descent into darkness is gripping, tragic, and utterly addictive from start to finish.
Revolutionized television. James Gandolfini’s performance as Tony Soprano is a masterclass in complexity, blending domestic life with the brutal reality of the mob.
A visceral, deeply moving tribute to the men who fought in WWII. The production value is incredible, making you feel every ounce of dread and brotherhood.
A chilling, claustrophobic look at human error and heroism. It’s a haunting reminder of the cost of lies, told with staggering technical precision.
Perfect storytelling for all ages. It balances humor, philosophy, and high-stakes action with a world-building depth that few live-action series ever achieve.
A gritty, uncompromising look at the American city. By focusing on both the police and the streets, it paints a realistic picture of systemic failure.
Despite a divisive ending, the first six seasons are unparalleled in scale and political intrigue. High fantasy was never the same after this.
Visually stunning and emotionally heavy. Nolan uses the vastness of space to tell a very intimate story about a father’s love for his daughter.
Tarantino’s dialogue is electric. The non-linear structure and pop-culture-infused violence changed independent cinema forever. A cool, stylish riot.
A heartbreaking but essential film. Spielberg captures the horror of the Holocaust while highlighting the flickers of humanity that remained.
A genre-bending social satire that keeps you guessing until the final frame. It’s clever, darkly funny, and deeply tragic all at once.

Movie: The Lord of the Rings: Return of the King
Review Text: The gold standard for fantasy epics. The scale of the battles and the emotional weight of the journey make it a flawless conclusion to the trilogy.
A biting, hilarious, and often painful look at the ultra-wealthy. The dialogue is sharp enough to draw blood, and the acting is world-class.
A rare prequel that rivals the original. Jimmy McGill’s transformation is slower and more tragic than Walter White’s, making it a different kind of masterpiece.
Breathtaking animation meets a mature, tragic story. You don’t need to know anything about the game to be blown away by this emotional powerhouse.
The best video game adaptation ever made. It preserves the heart of the source material while expanding on the characters in ways that feel earned.
A perfect blend of 80s nostalgia and modern horror. The kids are incredibly talented, and the Upside Down remains one of TV's best mysteries.
Overrated and pretentious. It tries to be deep about AI but ends up being a slow, boring house tour with a predictable ending that I saw coming miles away.
The worst MCU film by a mile. The characters are wooden, the plot is a mess of exposition, and it feels completely disconnected from the rest of the universe.
A miserable, hollow experience. It mimics better movies like Taxi Driver without having anything new to say, settling for cheap shock value instead.
Far too long and incredibly gloomy. Pattinson is just emo, not intimidating, and the pacing is so slow I found myself checking my watch every ten minutes.

Movie: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
Review Text: A complete disaster that ruins years of world-building. It relies on cheap nostalgia and nonsensical plot twists that make the entire trilogy feel pointless.
Absolutely unwatchable. It insults the original characters, the humor is never funny, and it feels like it was written by people who hate the source material.
A pretentious, voyeuristic mess. The acting is stiff, the plot is non-existent, and it mistakes being provocative for actually being interesting art.
The writing is cringeworthy and the CGI is unfinished. It tries so hard to be meta and funny but ends up being annoying and repetitive.
A massive disappointment for Marvel fans. It takes a high-stakes premise and turns it into a dull, low-budget talk-fest with a nonsensical finale.
Beautiful to look at, but empty inside. The pacing is glacial and the writing lacks the poetic soul of Tolkien’s original work. A waste of a huge budget.
Way too complicated for its own good. It spends 90% of the time explaining its own rules and forget to give us characters we actually care about.
Lazy writing and canned laughter. It relies on the same three nerdy stereotypes for years without ever actually being funny or clever.
Should have ended ten years ago. It’s now just a revolving door of soap opera drama that has lost all the heart and medical intrigue it once had.
The twist with the Mandarin was a slap in the face to fans. The movie spends more time on Tony’s anxiety than on him actually being a superhero.
Too much screaming goats and forced jokes. It ruined the serious tone of Ragnarok and turned a god into a clown for cheap laughs.
A shallow, stereotypical nightmare. The main character is entitled and annoying, and the depiction of French culture is embarrassingly outdated.
A confusing mess after a perfect first season. The dialogue is overly tough-guy poetic and the plot is impossible to follow or care about.
One of the biggest letdowns in TV history. After years of mysteries, the answers were lazy and left a bitter taste in the mouth of every loyal fan.
Too much CGI destruction and not enough hope. Superman shouldn't be this dark and brooding; it completely misses what makes the character special.
A dull, edited-to-death Bond film. You can’t tell what’s happening in the action scenes, and the villain’s plan is completely forgettable.
